cohort: The study included 134 inborn extreme preterm infants, born at <26 weeks' gestation and weighing <750 g, admitted to a tertiary-level NICU between 2002 and 2019.
finding: Over nearly two decades, survival among extreme preterm infants improved significantly, with antenatal corticosteroid administration and cesarean birth associated with increased survival, while early hypotension and severe IVH were predictors of mortality.
mod_finding: Cesarean birth was independently associated with increased odds of survival among extreme preterm infants.
